section-why.hook: Asha and Ben both use AI every day. Only one of the two gets home on time.

why-then.helps: Asha remembers the two-day features, so Asha knows which parts AI should speed up: the searching, the boilerplate and the first draft of the tests.
why-then.wrong: Ben assumes AI makes every step faster, even the thinking, and skips the parts that used to catch bugs: careful debugging and a real review.

diagram-then-now.helps: Asha hands the slow, repetitive parts to AI and still checks every change. The feature ships in a day, and nothing comes back.
diagram-then-now.wrong: Ben accepts the first answer to save time. The feature looks done by lunch, then takes two more days of debugging and rework.

why-research.helps: Asha reads the headline and the small print: the gains came from clear tasks, clear goals and developers checking the results.
why-research.wrong: Ben quotes the 56% to the team, expects it on every task, then can’t explain why the sprint still slips.

why-catch.helps: Asha times real work instead of trusting a feeling, and notices when a chat with AI costs more time than it saves.
why-catch.wrong: Ben feels faster with AI, so Ben never checks. In the study, that feeling was wrong by almost 40 percentage points.

why-factors.helps: Asha checks five things before every task: focused context, a clear prompt, the right mode, a careful review and an eye on the cost.
why-factors.wrong: Ben relies on the model being clever. Without the five habits, a clever model just produces confident mistakes faster.

why-handover.helps: Asha is on the right side of the line, and it isn’t talent. It is five habits, practised until each one is automatic.
why-handover.wrong: Ben is on the wrong side, working hard and staying late. Nothing in this session is harder than Ben’s current routine.

section-key-terms.hook: Ben nodded along when someone said “context window”. Asha asked what it meant.

diagram-request.helps: Asha knows each request sends the whole context again, so Asha keeps it lean, and every answer stays fast and sharp.
diagram-request.wrong: Ben thinks Copilot remembers the project between chats. It doesn’t, so Ben’s answers keep missing details that were never sent.

key-terms-cards-0.helps: Asha leaves the model on Auto for everyday work and writes a clear prompt. Simple tasks come back quickly and cost little.
key-terms-cards-0.wrong: Ben picks the biggest reasoning model to rename a variable. It thinks for a minute and costs several times more for the same result.

key-terms-cards-1.helps: Asha attaches only the two files that matter. Fewer tokens on the whiteboard means quicker, sharper answers.
key-terms-cards-1.wrong: Ben attaches the whole folder “just in case”. The context window fills with noise, and the answer misses the actual bug.

key-terms-cards-2.helps: Asha starts a fresh chat for each task, so the history holds only what matters and every tool result is relevant.
key-terms-cards-2.wrong: Ben keeps one chat for the whole week. Every prompt drags along days of history, and the agent keeps mixing up tasks.

key-terms-cards-3.helps: Asha checks any unfamiliar function against the docs before using it, and glances at the credits used once a day.
key-terms-cards-3.wrong: Ben trusts a confident answer that calls a function that doesn’t exist, then spends an afternoon and a pile of credits chasing it.

section-mental-model.hook: Ben’s chat has been open since Monday. Asha starts a fresh one for every task.

mental-model-cards-0.helps: Asha attaches one test file with #selection instead of pasting 400 lines. Every prompt starts small and stays on topic.
mental-model-cards-0.wrong: Ben asks about the API in a chat full of CSS. The old turns ride along, and the answer drifts back to styling.

mental-model-cards-1.helps: Asha keeps the instruction file to 30 lines and asks the agent for just the summary line of the test run.
mental-model-cards-1.wrong: Ben’s 600-line instruction file rides along with every prompt, and a full test log follows it. Every question pays for both.

mental-model-cards-2.helps: Asha glances at the context window control and compacts at half full, while the details are still sharp.
mental-model-cards-2.wrong: Ben ignores the control until it fills. Automatic compaction kicks in, and the morning’s decisions get fuzzy.

diagram-context-stack.helps: Asha knows the history grows with every prompt, so Asha asks for short replies and starts fresh between tasks.
diagram-context-stack.wrong: Ben’s fourth prompt sends nearly four times the tokens of the first, for a one-line question. Ben pays for the whole pile.

facts-mental-model.helps: Asha drags a screenshot of the broken layout straight into the chat. One picture replaces a paragraph of description.
facts-mental-model.wrong: Ben describes the layout bug in three paragraphs, and Copilot fixes the wrong element twice.

section-prompt-cost.hook: Asha types one careful prompt. Ben types five quick ones, and pays for every one.

diagram-snowball.helps: Asha names the files, the symptom and the test. Two rounds, one fix, done before the coffee cools.
diagram-snowball.wrong: Ben types “fix the login bug” and spends five rounds steering. Each round re-sends everything before it, so the cost snowballs.

diagram-anatomy.helps: Asha’s prompt has five parts: where, symptom, evidence, limits and done when. Copilot has nothing left to guess.
diagram-anatomy.wrong: Ben leaves out the limits. Copilot “helpfully” rewrites three other files, and the review takes longer than the fix.

section-modes.hook: Asha asks before changing anything. Ben lets the agent loose on every question.

diagram-modes.helps: Asha climbs only as high as the task needs: Ask to understand, Plan to agree, Agent to change.
diagram-modes.wrong: Ben uses Agent for everything, even questions. Simple answers arrive with file edits nobody asked for, and a bigger bill.

mode-ask.helps: Asha uses Ask to understand a tricky hook before touching it. Nothing changes, and the answer costs little.
mode-ask.wrong: Ben asks the agent why a component re-renders and gets an answer plus three edited files to undo.

mode-plan.helps: Asha asks for a plan, spots a wrong assumption in line three, and fixes it with one sentence.
mode-plan.wrong: Ben skips the plan. The agent builds the wrong design across eight files, and Ben throws the whole run away.

mode-agent.helps: Asha gives the agent one agreed step, the files and the test to run. The change is small and easy to review.
mode-agent.wrong: Ben tells the agent “build the feature”. It reads half the project, edits twenty files and burns through credits.

mode-edit.helps: Asha reads an old guide, sees “Edit mode” and simply uses Agent instead.
mode-edit.wrong: Ben spends twenty minutes hunting for Edit mode, then switches a hidden setting back on instead of just using Agent.

section-cheat-sheet.hook: Ben pastes logs into the chat. Asha types # and picks exactly what Copilot needs.

diagram-prefixes.helps: Asha types # and picks #problems instead of pasting errors. Copilot gets exactly the errors, nothing more.
diagram-prefixes.wrong: Ben pastes the whole terminal output, warnings and all. Copilot chases a harmless warning instead of the real error.

cheat-slash-0.helps: Asha types /clear between tasks. Each new task starts on a clean whiteboard, cheap and focused.
cheat-slash-0.wrong: Ben never clears. The CSS chat from Monday is still steering Thursday’s database answers.

cheat-slash-1.helps: Asha selects the function and types /tests. The tests arrive next to the code, ready to review.
cheat-slash-1.wrong: Ben describes the function in a paragraph and asks for tests. Copilot guesses which function, and tests the wrong one.

cheat-slash-2.helps: Asha runs /init in a new repo and gets a starter instruction file in a minute.
cheat-slash-2.wrong: Ben writes the same project rules into every prompt by hand, and forgets a different one each time.

cheat-slash-3.helps: Asha runs /review-changes, the team’s saved prompt, before every pull request. Same checks every time, in one word.
cheat-slash-3.wrong: Ben retypes a long review prompt from memory, and quietly drops a different check each time.

cheat-context-0.helps: Asha types #problems instead of copying compiler errors. Copilot sees the exact errors, with file and line.
cheat-context-0.wrong: Ben retypes an error message from memory, gets one word wrong, and Copilot fixes a problem that doesn’t exist.

cheat-context-1.helps: Asha selects the three error lines and uses #terminalSelection. The prompt stays tiny and on point.
cheat-context-1.wrong: Ben copies 1,500 lines of build log into the chat. Every later prompt pays for that log again.

cheat-context-2.helps: Asha knows where the code lives, so Asha attaches the file directly and saves #codebase for genuine unknowns.
cheat-context-2.wrong: Ben uses #codebase for everything. Each search pulls in dozens of snippets and slows every answer.

cheat-participant-0.helps: Asha asks @terminal for a shell command and gets an answer in the right syntax first time.
cheat-participant-0.wrong: Ben asks a general chat for a PowerShell command and gets a bash answer to translate by hand.

cheat-shortcut-0.helps: Asha opens inline chat on the selection for small edits. Tiny context, instant answer.
cheat-shortcut-0.wrong: Ben opens the full Chat view, explains which function, pastes it in and waits. For a two-line change.

cheat-shortcut-1.helps: Asha accepts a suggestion one word at a time when only half of it is right.
cheat-shortcut-1.wrong: Ben accepts the whole grey suggestion with Tab, then deletes half of it. Every time.

cheat-setting-0.helps: Asha hovers the context window control before a big question and compacts first if it is past half.
cheat-setting-0.wrong: Ben has never noticed the control. The window fills, compaction kicks in, and early decisions quietly disappear.

cheat-setting-1.helps: Asha reopens yesterday’s chat from the sessions list instead of explaining the whole bug again.
cheat-setting-1.wrong: Ben starts a new chat and re-explains the bug from scratch, then attaches the same files all over again.

facts-cheat-sheet.helps: Asha pops chat into its own window on the second monitor. Code on one screen, conversation on the other.
facts-cheat-sheet.wrong: Ben squeezes chat into a narrow sidebar and scrolls back and forth all day.

section-workflow.hook: Asha follows the same seven steps every time. Ben improvises, and it shows.

diagram-daily-loop.helps: Asha runs the same loop for every task and ends with commit, then clear. The next task always starts clean.
diagram-daily-loop.wrong: Ben skips steps when busy, which is always. Tasks blur into one long chat and one huge commit.

workflow-steps-0.helps: Asha starts each task with /clear, picks the role and attaches two files. Set-up takes ten seconds.
workflow-steps-0.wrong: Ben continues yesterday’s chat on Agent with the biggest model. The first answer is slow, expensive and confused.

workflow-steps-1.helps: Asha agrees a plan, then builds one step at a time with a test run after each. Problems show up while small.
workflow-steps-1.wrong: Ben asks for everything at once. Forty changed files later, the tests fail and nobody knows which change broke the build.

workflow-steps-2.helps: Asha reads every line of the diff, commits small, then clears. Any bad change is one commit away from undone.
workflow-steps-2.wrong: Ben skims the diff and commits a day’s work at once. Finding the line that broke production takes the next morning.

diagram-chat-flow.helps: When a chat gets long, Asha asks two questions: has the task changed, and is the window half full? The answers say what to do.
diagram-chat-flow.wrong: Ben keeps going no matter what. Answers get vaguer, slower and pricier, and Ben blames the model.

workflow-cards-0.helps: Asha compacts with a focus, “keep the API contract”, so the summary keeps what matters.
workflow-cards-0.wrong: Ben argues with a confused chat for an hour instead of starting over with one clear prompt.

facts-workflow.helps: Asha sees the agent heading the wrong way and steers it mid-task, without losing the work so far.
facts-workflow.wrong: Ben waits for the agent to finish a wrong approach, then asks it to undo everything.

section-dos-donts.hook: Small habits, big difference: here is what Asha does and Ben doesn’t.

dd-context-cost-0.helps: Asha’s chats are short and focused, so each prompt carries little and costs little.
dd-context-cost-0.wrong: Ben’s day-long chat means every small question pays for hours of old conversation.

dd-context-cost-1.helps: Asha attaches files directly and lets an everyday model do everyday work.
dd-context-cost-1.wrong: Ben reaches for #codebase and the biggest model out of habit, and the monthly bill shows it.

dd-prompting-0.helps: Asha writes the goal, the limits and “done when” into every prompt, and saves the best ones as prompt files.
dd-prompting-0.wrong: Ben types “make it better”. Copilot guesses what better means, and Ben spends three rounds explaining.

dd-prompting-1.helps: Asha asks for replies in five lines. The answers are quicker to read and cheaper to carry forward.
dd-prompting-1.wrong: Ben corrects the same mistake a third time in a muddled chat. The wrong attempts keep pulling the answer back.

dd-reviewing-0.helps: Asha asks Copilot to run the tests and show the result, then reads the diff before committing.
dd-reviewing-0.wrong: Ben ships a package name the model invented. The build breaks in CI, in front of the whole team.

dd-security-0.helps: Asha keeps tool approvals on and uses fake data in prompts. Nothing leaves the machine that shouldn’t.
dd-security-0.wrong: Ben pastes a real customer record to reproduce a bug and turns on global auto-approve. One afternoon, two policy breaches.

facts-dos-donts.helps: Asha restores a checkpoint to undo a bad edit, and still commits often, because a checkpoint can’t undo commands.
facts-dos-donts.wrong: Ben trusts Restore Checkpoint to undo a migration the agent already ran. The files rewind; the database doesn’t.

section-team-memory.hook: Ben types “use our logger” in every prompt. Asha wrote it down once.

diagram-memory.helps: Asha puts the SQL rules in a file that only applies to migrations. React work never pays for those rules.
diagram-memory.wrong: Ben puts every rule for every language in the always-on file. Each prompt carries pages of rules it doesn’t need.

team-memory-cards-0.helps: Asha writes the team’s rules once in a short instruction file. Every teammate’s Copilot follows the rules from then on.
team-memory-cards-0.wrong: Ben types “use the logger, not console.log” in every prompt, and forgets it on the one that matters.

team-memory-cards-1.helps: Asha creates a read-only reviewer agent. It can search and read but never edit, so reviews stay safe.
team-memory-cards-1.wrong: Ben keeps AGENTS.md and copilot-instructions.md saying slightly different things. Copilot gets both, and contradicts itself.

facts-team-memory.helps: Asha shares a Space with the team’s design docs, so everyone’s Copilot starts from the same context.
facts-team-memory.wrong: Ben pastes the same design doc into chat every week, for every teammate who asks.

section-templates.hook: Asha keeps a drawer of prompts that work. Ben starts from a blank box every time.

tpl-bug.helps: Asha asks for a failing test first, then the fix. The test proves the bug is really gone.
tpl-bug.wrong: Ben asks for a fix with no test. The bug returns two weeks later, and a customer spots it first.

tpl-feature.helps: Asha’s plan prompt names the users, the musts and the must-nots. The plan arrives in twenty lines and fits the real need.
tpl-feature.wrong: Ben asks for a feature in one line and gets a plan for a different feature.

tpl-refactor.helps: Asha runs the tests before and after the refactor and compares the summary lines. Same behaviour, cleaner code.
tpl-refactor.wrong: Ben refactors without a test run, and a quiet behaviour change ships with the tidy code.

tpl-tests.helps: Asha names the edge cases that matter. The tests cover expired links, not just the happy path.
tpl-tests.wrong: Ben asks for “some tests” and gets five copies of the obvious one.

tpl-explain.helps: Asha asks for inputs, outputs and side effects in ten lines. Unfamiliar code makes sense in five minutes.
tpl-explain.wrong: Ben asks “what does this do?” and gets a 600-word essay that buries the one surprising side effect.

tpl-review.helps: Asha runs a saved review prompt before every pull request and fixes the two real issues it finds.
tpl-review.wrong: Ben opens the pull request straight away. A reviewer finds the same two issues a day later.

tpl-error.helps: Asha hands over #terminalLastCommand and asks for the root cause. The fix comes with a re-run as proof.
tpl-error.wrong: Ben describes the error from memory, gets a fix for a different error, and applies it anyway.

tpl-commit.helps: Asha lets Copilot draft the commit message from #changes, then edits it to say why.
tpl-commit.wrong: Ben commits with “wip” for the fifth time today. Nobody, including Ben, can tell what changed.

facts-templates.helps: Asha edits an earlier prompt instead of arguing. VS Code rewinds the changes from that point and tries again.
facts-templates.wrong: Ben piles correction on correction, and the bad first attempt stays in the chat, steering every answer.

section-quiz.hook: Your turn: what would Asha do?

section-security.hook: Ben clicked “always allow” to save time. Asha still reads every command.

diagram-approval.helps: Asha reads each command before allowing it, and allows routine ones for the session only.
diagram-approval.wrong: Ben switched on global auto-approve on day one. The agent then ran a clean-up script on the wrong folder.

security-cards-0.helps: Asha swaps the real API key for a placeholder before asking for help. Copilot fixes the loading code just the same.
security-cards-0.wrong: Ben pastes the .env file to show the problem. The key has to be rotated, and the incident report takes longer than the bug.

security-cards-1.helps: Asha keeps the agent away from excluded folders and checks the licence when code referencing flags a match.
security-cards-1.wrong: Ben assumes content exclusion protects the payments folder in Agent mode. It doesn’t.

facts-security.helps: Asha installs MCP servers only from sources the team trusts, after reading what each one can do.
facts-security.wrong: Ben installs the first MCP server a blog recommends. It can run any code on Ben’s laptop.

section-beyond.hook: Copilot drafts Asha’s commit messages. Ben still types “fix stuff”.

beyond-cards-0.helps: Asha describes a shell command in plain words in the terminal and checks it before running.
beyond-cards-0.wrong: Ben searches the web for the right flags, copies a command from a forum and runs it unchecked.

beyond-cards-1.helps: Asha assigns a small, well-described issue to the cloud agent and reviews its pull request over coffee.
beyond-cards-1.wrong: Ben hands the cloud agent a vague issue called “improve performance” and gets back a pull request nobody can review.

facts-beyond.helps: Asha clicks Explain error on a failing check and has the cause in a minute.
facts-beyond.wrong: Ben scrolls through 3,000 lines of CI log looking for the one red line.

section-wrap-up.hook: Seven habits separate Asha’s week from Ben’s.

summary.helps: Asha picks one habit a week, starting with /clear between tasks. By the end of the month, all seven are automatic.
summary.wrong: Ben tries to change everything at once on Monday, and is back to old habits by Wednesday.
